content.value_statement: Conflicting objectives make algorithm selection, constraint handling, and trade-off analysis difficult. This skill provides practical pymoo workflows, examples, and reference guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains single, multi-objective, many-objective, and constrained optimization workflows.
Guides selection among GA, DE, PSO, NSGA-II, NSGA-III, MOEA/D, and related methods.
Shows how to define custom ElementwiseProblem objectives, bounds, and constraints.
Demonstrates benchmark problems from the ZDT, DTLZ, WFG, and single-objective families.
Covers Pareto-front visualization and preference-based solution selection.
Provides runnable examples for optimization, constraints, and multi-criteria decision making.
limitations: Requires Python and a compatible pymoo 0.6.x installation.
Example parameters are starting points and require validation for each problem.
The skill does not guarantee global optimality or convergence.
Interactive plots may require a graphical environment or notebook backend.

use_cases.title: Compare Engineering Designs
use_cases.description: Model cost, weight, and performance objectives, then inspect feasible Pareto-optimal designs.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Evolutionary Algorithms
use_cases.description: Run reproducible comparisons on ZDT or DTLZ problems using suitable algorithms and termination criteria.

use_cases.title: Teach Pareto Optimization
use_cases.description: Use focused examples to explain conflicting objectives, constraints, Pareto fronts, and preference-based selection.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starting Algorithm
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a pymoo algorithm for [objective count], [variable type], and [constraints]. Explain the choice and suggest initial population and termination settings.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Custom Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a pymoo ElementwiseProblem for [objectives], [bounds], and [constraints]. Check objective direction and convert inequalities to the required form.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Optimization Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these convergence statistics and Pareto results: [results]. Identify scaling, feasibility, diversity, or termination issues and recommend controlled experiments.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Validation Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reproducible comparison of [algorithms] on [problem]. Define seeds, budgets, indicators, constraint metrics, visualizations, and decision criteria.

output_examples.input: Select an algorithm for three continuous objectives with inequality constraints.
output_examples.output: Start with NSGA-II and feasibility-first handling. Use a moderate population, fixed seed, normalized objectives, and track feasible Pareto diversity.

output_examples.input: Explain why a many-objective result has poor coverage.
output: Check whether reference directions match the objective count.
Increase evaluations while holding the random seed strategy constant.
Normalize objectives and inspect duplicate or infeasible solutions.

output_examples.input: Choose one design from a two-objective Pareto front.
output_examples.output: Normalize both objectives, document preference weights, apply pseudo-weights, and compare the selected design with both extreme solutions.

best_practices: Set random seeds and compare multiple runs before drawing conclusions.
Normalize objectives when scales differ and report feasibility separately.
Match algorithms, operators, and termination criteria to variable and objective structure.
anti_patterns: Do not treat one stochastic run as reliable evidence.
Do not compare algorithms with different evaluation budgets.
Do not select a Pareto solution before documenting stakeholder preferences.

faq.question: Does this skill support single-objective optimization?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers GA, DE, PSO, CMA-ES, benchmark problems, termination settings, and result inspection.

faq.question: Which algorithm should I use for two objectives?
faq.answer: NSGA-II is a practical baseline. Problem structure, constraints, evaluation cost, and desired diversity may justify another method.

faq.question: How are inequality constraints represented?
faq.answer: Represent each inequality so feasible values are less than or equal to zero.

faq.question: Can it handle five or more objectives?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers NSGA-III, reference directions, and parallel-coordinate visualization for many-objective problems.

faq.question: Are the included examples production-ready?
faq.answer: No. They are educational baselines that require domain validation, parameter tuning, testing, and resource planning.

faq.question: Does the skill install pymoo automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents an explicit installation command, but users control whether they run it.
